title: Maxime Saury and Claude Bolling gone commercial
summary: She says Saury and Luter lead the commercial New Orleans orchestras in Paris, and describes Claude Bolling as a gifted pianist now doing film music and Brigitte Bardot accompaniments.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: What happened to people like Maxim Sari? What is he doing now?

Oh, he is very commercial. He is a very proud. He plays well with the clarinet. And he does good arrangements, I believe, because he has done long studies in the music Conservatory of Paris. But he lives with his music, and it's really quite commercial. But it's not bad, when he comes to the music. Well, he is certainly in the orchestra, in the only, in the two commercial orchestras, in the Nouvelle Orléans, in Paris, there is him and Luther, and I think that now, he is better than Luther, as well. Because Luther is not what he was.
Do you know, I don't know how to pronounce it. Claude Boling?

Claude Boling, oh, yes. Claude Boling, he is a wonderful pianist. He is also very, very proud. He has done extraordinary things. I met him when he was 14 years old. He was a little boy. He played piano in the surprise party, in the cassette of his parents, because he was not right. He was already a piano player. And he did his first orchestra, which was already very good, and which was at this moment, in a very New Orleans style, which was practically the same, that the style of Maxime Sorrie, and of Claude Luther. It was in 1950, but he has terribly changed, because he also, like Sorrie, he also lives his music. And he also does arrangements. He does music of films. He does music of a film, the Brigitte Bardot, and he accompanies Brigitte Bardot when she sings. And now he has a kind of a chorus of singers with him, with the girls who call them the Parisians, and who sing in the style Charleston, something of that kind. And it's very, very commercial. And it's not good at all. It's a shame, because he was a very proud musician.
